title: When the Hymn Wakes
premise: Ivo Lockridge, a skeptical urban explorer documenting the flooded quarry tunnels beneath his dying hometown of Marrow's Bend, discovers a survey-impossible passage sealed by a door locked from within. When an excavation crew breaches it, something that was invited in generations ago wakes, and Ivo is trapped underground with four strangers as the water begins to rise. To survive until sunrise he must piece together his grandmother's hymnal and the town's buried covenant: the thing below was sung in, and only a true heir can sing it back to sleep. In the end Ivo, who has never believed, accepts the inheritance he fled — sings the waking hymn with his found family holding the light — and seals the door from the inside, choosing to stay behind as the well refills.
about_author: Rosalind Sandoval is a former church archivist from rural Pennsylvania who spent a decade cataloging hymnals and funeral records before turning to horror. She writes about small towns that keep their promises too literally.

chapters.title: The Survey Says Nothing
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He maps the quarry tunnels for one last video before selling his late grandmother's house, mocking local superstitions on camera. He finds a corridor his laser measure insists doesn't exist. Emotional beat: restless detachment masking grief he refuses to name.

chapters.title: A Door Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The excavation crew, tipped off by his footage, breaches a rusted door whose bolts are thrown from within. The air tastes of candle smoke. That night every dog in Marrow's Bend faces the quarry and howls. Beat: first crack in his skepticism; dread arrives as logistics.

chapters.title: Descend
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, intercut with crew foreman Dara's journal entries. The crew goes missing below; Ivo descends to film a rescue and finds them standing in a circle, singing a hymn he half-remembers from childhood. Beat: the past reaching up through memory.

chapters.title: Four Strangers and a Rising Well
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV shifts. Ivo, Dara, teenage runaway Kit, and retired teacher Mr. Okafor are sealed in when the tunnel floods behind them. They find a dry chapel chamber with pews facing a wellhead. Beat: terror forging reluctant fellowship.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. He reveals the town covenant: in 1911 the founders sang something up from the water to save their dying crops, then locked it away and swore each generation to forget. The hymnal pages were torn out and scattered. Beat: inheritance as burden, not gift.

chapters.title: The Hymnal in Her Handwriting
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Among the chapel debris he finds his grandmother's hymnal, her handwriting filling the torn pages — she was the last singer, and she left it where he would find it. The thing below begins calling them by name in their loved ones' voices. Beat: grief weaponized against him.

chapters.title: Kit Sings First
chapters.summary: Kit's POV. The entity lures Kit with her mother's voice toward the wellhead; Ivo pulls her back, but the water rises faster now, hours ahead of sunrise. Dara is taken while holding the light. Beat: found family solidifying through loss.

chapters.title: The Truth About Believing
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cornered and drowning-adjacent, Ivo admits what he's always known: he heard the hymn as a boy and forgot on purpose, like everyone. Belief was never the requirement — willingness was. Beat: surrender of the skeptic's armor.

chapters.title: Sunrise Is a Doorway
chapters.summary: Climax, rotating POVs. As dawn bleeds through fissures above, Ivo, Kit, and Okafor sing the waking hymn together, voices braided, holding the light while the well churns. The entity surfaces as everything they've lost at once. Beat: terror transfigured into communion.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: Resolution, Ivo's POV. The hymn ends; the water recedes to a whisper. Ivo sends Kit and Okafor up, throws the bolt himself, and sits in the dark with the hymnal open, keeping the promise his grandmother kept. Above, two survivors tell a town that chooses, once more, to forget. Beat: inheritance accepted; quiet, terrible peace.
